resources.string: Since the last cleanup (%1$s), probably after a system update: %2$s app(s) back on, %3$s setting(s) changed back.
%1$s choices ticked again, with the values you chose before. Press Apply to turn them off again.
Fire TV: some of Amazon\'s apps stay on
Fire OS protects some of Amazon\'s apps, so only the Amazon parts known to switch off safely are listed below. You can also turn off Amazon\'s tracking in the TV\'s own menu.
Still on: %1$s. On the TV, open Settings → Preferences → Privacy Settings and turn them off.
Amazon\'s tracking switches are all off.
The TV\'s maker doesn\'t allow switching this off.
On a Fire TV: Settings → My Fire TV → About, press OK on the device name 7 times, then go back to Developer options and turn on ADB debugging.
How the TV is doing right now. Nothing is changed.
%1$s: on average %2$s tasks want the processor, which has %3$s cores. On for %4$s.
The apps and system parts holding the most memory right now.
Memory is short. On the list, \"Freeze apps left in the background\" and \"Keep fewer apps in memory\" help.
Storage is nearly full. On the list, \"Free up storage\" clears app caches.
The processor is busy even at rest. Something may be running in the background; a crash loop below would explain it.
%1$s keeps crashing and restarting (%2$s times in the recent log). It is a system part that must stay on: tell the maker or your operator.
%1$s keeps crashing and restarting (%2$s times in the recent log). You can turn it off from the list.
%1$s keeps crashing and restarting (%2$s times in the recent log).
Nothing to worry about: memory, storage and processor look fine, and nothing is crashing.
Software, updates and security of the TV. Nothing changes unless you press a button.
Open System update on the TV
System update is open on the TV.
About is open on the TV (My Fire TV on Fire TV): System update and Reset are in it, or one level up.
Settings are open on the TV.
The last security update is recent.
The last security update is %1$s months old. Open System update to look for a newer one.
The last security update is %1$s months old. If System update finds nothing newer, the TV may no longer get security fixes from its maker: install only well-known apps on it.
The bootloader is locked and Android is checked at every start: the TV runs its original, unmodified software.
The bootloader is unlocked: the TV\'s software can be replaced, and streaming apps may refuse to play in HD.
Android isn\'t the maker\'s original software (verified boot: %1$s).
Other software, signed with its own key
Unlocking the bootloader erases the TV and can stop streaming apps from playing in HD. This app doesn\'t do it.
A normal restart, which often cures a slow or stuck TV. The app waits for it and connects again once it is back.
Restart the TV now? Whatever is playing stops.
Restarting the TV, waiting for it to come back (up to 4 minutes)…
The TV is back and connected again.
The TV didn\'t come back within 4 minutes. Once it is on, connect it again from the Connect step.

Erases everything on the TV: apps, accounts and settings. Only the TV itself can do it: look for Reset under About (in Device Preferences or System, depending on the TV). On Fire TV: My Fire TV, Reset to Factory Defaults.
Which apps can use the microphone, a camera, your location and personal data. Remove what an app doesn\'t need.
Removing an access closes the app if it is open, and it can ask again the next time it needs it. Each removal is saved: undo it from Restore.
No app has these accesses, apart from the ones the TV needs.
Can record sound, from the remote\'s microphone or the TV\'s own.
Can take photos and videos with a camera built into or plugged into the TV.
Can see where the TV is even when the app isn\'t open. Removing this keeps location while you use the app.
Can see where the TV is, from its network. Removing this also removes \"all the time\".
Can read and change the contacts of the TV\'s Google account.
Can read and change your calendar.
The apps you installed: how much space each one takes and where it came from. Open, stop, turn off or uninstall them from here.
Turning an app off hides it and stops it running, with nothing deleted; turn it back on here or from Restore. Uninstalling deletes the app and its data from the TV.
You haven\'t installed any apps on this TV.
%1$s app(s) didn\'t come from Google Play or the Amazon Appstore. That\'s fine if you installed them yourself; if you don\'t know where they came from, look at them closely.
Show its settings on the TV
Uninstall %1$s? The app and everything it stored on the TV are deleted. This can\'t be undone from Restore.
The settings for %1$s are open on the TV.
%1$s was stopped. It starts again when you open it.
%1$s is turned off. Undo it here or from Restore.
Install an Android TV app from this phone, for example on a TV without the Play Store.
%1$s is installed. Find it in the TV\'s apps list.
Only install apps from sources you trust. An app can see everything you do on the TV.
See what the TV shows and control it from here.
Films and series from streaming apps show as black: they are protected from screenshots.
Keyboard: arrows, Enter = OK, Backspace = Back, H = Home.
UnbloatMyTV %1$s is out; you have %2$s. Updating takes a few seconds and the app restarts by itself. Your backups are kept.
Check for updates automatically when the app starts
The app is working on your TV. Update once it has finished.
The download doesn\'t match the published file, so it was thrown away. Nothing was changed.
GitHub couldn\'t be reached. Check the internet connection and try again later.
Make your TV quick and private again
This app turns off the ads, tracking and preinstalled apps you don\'t use, then checks the TV still works. It takes about five minutes and you decide every change.
Apps are switched off, not uninstalled. A factory reset brings everything back too.
Every change is saved on this phone first, so you can put it back exactly as it was.
Safe choices are ticked for you. Anything you might use is left for you to decide.
Before you start, on the TV
Open Settings → Device Preferences → About. On Google TV: Settings → System → About.
Scroll to “Build” (or “Android TV OS build”) and press OK on it 7 times, until the TV says you are a developer.
Go back one screen, open Developer options and turn on USB debugging. If you also see “Network debugging” or “ADB over network”, turn that on too.
Leave the TV on, connected to the same home network as this phone.

Works with Android TV and Google TV (TVs, streaming boxes, sticks and operator set-top boxes) and with Fire TV, where Amazon\'s own apps can\'t be switched off. Samsung (Tizen), LG (webOS), Roku and Apple TV run other systems and are not supported.
Google\'s Android tools (ADB) are installed for this app. Nothing else is needed.
The app will download Google\'s official Android tools (ADB, about 7 MB) when you press Continue. They stay inside this app\'s folder; nothing is installed on the system.
The download failed: %1$s\nCheck that this phone is online and try again.
The TV and this phone need to be on the same network. Search for it, or type its address.
Looks for TVs with network debugging turned on. Takes about ten seconds.
No TV answered. Check that USB debugging (and Network debugging, if your TV has it) is on, then search again or type the address below.
On the TV: Settings → Network & Internet → select your network. The address looks like 192.168.1.20.
Reading what is on the TV…
It is asking “Allow USB debugging?”. Tick “Always allow from this computer” and choose OK. No message? Turn USB debugging off and on again in Developer options.
Check that the TV is on, that USB debugging is still on, and that the address is right. Some TVs turn debugging off after a restart.
That doesn\'t look like an address. It should look like 192.168.1.20.
The TV at %1$s did not accept the connection.
The TV didn\'t allow the connection in time. Try again and accept the message on the TV.
My TV shows “Wireless debugging” with a pairing code

Newer Google TV devices: in Developer options open Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code. Type the address with its port and the 6-digit code shown, then connect with the address shown on the Wireless debugging screen.
Type the address with its port (like 192.168.1.20:37099) and the 6-digit code.
Paired. Now type the address shown on the Wireless debugging screen above and connect.
Pairing failed. Check the code; it changes each time.
TVs this phone connected to before. Debugging must still be on for them.
Only things found on this TV are listed. Recommended choices are already ticked and don\'t change how you watch TV.
Restart the TV afterwards and check that everything works (recommended)
%1$s choices made on %2$s (%3$s). Anything this TV doesn\'t have is skipped.
%1$s choices ticked. %2$s aren\'t on this TV and were skipped.
That file doesn\'t contain saved choices.

This TV has %1$s preinstalled apps the list doesn\'t know yet. Suggesting them on GitHub helps add the useless ones for everyone. Only the TV model and app names are included, and you see everything before posting.
Keep the TV on. This usually takes one to three minutes.
Your TV is cleaned up and the checks passed.
%1$s step(s) didn\'t work; see below. Everything else was applied, and you can undo it from Restore.
Saving a backup on this phone
The TV didn\'t come back within 4 minutes. It may have turned debugging off; your changes are still applied.
Home screen opens, internet and name lookups work.
No home screen answers. Use Restore to undo the last run.
The TV can\'t reach the internet.
The TV is online but can\'t look up names. Undo the DNS change from Restore.
Names stopped resolving with this DNS, so the previous setting was put back.
One last step on the TV

Turn debugging off once you are done. While it is on, other devices on your network can ask to control the TV. This app can do it for you, or turn off USB debugging (and Network debugging) yourself in Developer options. Turn it on again whenever you want to use this app.
Debugging is off and this app is disconnected. To use it again, turn USB debugging back on in Developer options.
The TV is still answering, so this didn\'t work on this model. Turn off USB debugging in Developer options on the TV instead.
What was done, step by step
Left on: another choice you made needs it.
Everything that was changed, with the original values, is saved here. The Restore page uses it to undo.
Undo a previous run on this TV. Apps come back and every setting returns to what it was before.
No saved runs for this TV on this phone.
Apps turned off: %1$s · settings changed: %2$s · accesses removed: %3$s
Undone. The apps are back and the settings are as they were.
A safety net, even without a backup: turns back on every app that was switched off by hand on this TV, including by other tools. Apps the manufacturer disabled itself are left alone.
Optional: a home screen without ads

The home screen is the one thing this app never turns off, because the TV needs one. If its ads and suggestions still bother you, install another home screen from the Play Store. All of these are free.
Open in Play Store on the TV
Go back to the original home screen
On Google TV the Home button keeps opening Google\'s home screen. Projectivy can take over the button: in its settings, turn on “Override current launcher”.
The Play Store page for %1$s is open on the TV. Install it with the remote, then press “Check again”.
The Play Store didn\'t open on the TV. Search for the app in the Play Store with the remote.
%1$s is now the home screen. Press Home on the remote to try it.
%1$s is now the default home screen. Open it once from the apps list to finish setting it up.
This TV kept its home screen. Open %1$s from the apps list; it can offer to take over from there.
The original home screen is back.
The TV didn\'t switch back. Uninstalling the other home screen also brings the original back.
This phone isn\'t on Wi-Fi. Connect it to the same network as the TV, then search again.
You can lock the phone or use other apps meanwhile: it carries on. Keep the phone on the same Wi-Fi.
Connect a TV to use the tools.
This TV uses Wireless debugging and doesn\'t know this phone yet. Pair it with a code below; the phone then connects by itself.
Newer Google TV devices: in Developer options open Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code. The address fills itself in when the phone sees that screen; type the 6-digit code and tap Pair.
Looking for the TV\'s pairing screen…
UnbloatMyTV %1$s is out; you have %2$s. Android asks you to confirm, then open the app again. Your choices and backups are kept.
Android needs your permission first: allow UnbloatMyTV to install apps, come back, and tap Install the update again.
Backups are kept inside this app, and uninstalling it deletes them. Save a copy elsewhere (Drive, a computer…) to be able to undo later anyway.
The copy couldn\'t be saved there.
Backup from %1$s added: it can be undone below.
This file isn\'t an UnbloatMyTV backup, or it has no changes in it.
This backup belongs to another TV (%1$s). Connect that TV to undo it.
%1$s apps are installed in other profiles on this device (a work profile or another person); they aren\'t listed here.
